theorems.statement: For a complete split-affine real-root certificate with fixed declared rational root r and fixed multiplicity, r is the smallest real root iff every other affine real-root branch h_j satisfies h_j>r. The selector-stable set is therefore an intersection of strict rational affine half-spaces.

For a complete split-affine real-root certificate with fixed declared rational root r>0 and fixed multiplicity, r is the smallest positive root iff every other affine real-root branch satisfies h_j<=0 or h_j>r. The selector-stable set is a finite Boolean combination of rational affine order inequalities and may be disconnected.

negative_boundaries.statement: T60/T61 require an exact complete real-root inventory; T59 declared validity alone is insufficient.
T60/T61 do not classify non-split parametric root-order chambers.
At a root collision the selector value may remain unchanged while the declared root multiplicity and Newton schedule become invalid.
Smallest-real and smallest-positive selectors have different order semantics and chamber boundaries.
A zero root does not displace a positive selected root under smallest-positive semantics.
Multiplying several moving affine root factors can create nonlinear parameter dependence in polynomial coefficients.
T60/T61 order conditions must be intersected with the T59 declared root/multiplicity/scale validity stratum.
The split selector certificate is not a complete Puiseux solver or generic multi-generator algebraic field.
